newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama gov't evaluating entry to cellphone market.
newsitem.headline: Panama gov't evaluating entry to cellphone market.

text.p: The Panamanian government is divided on when it should enter the cellular telephone market, a high-ranking government source said Tuesday.
The second of two cellular telephone bands is expected to be sold as a package with the sale of 49 percent of Panama's National Telecommunications Institute (INTEL).
However, government officials are divided on whether to have the cellular telephone band operating before the INTEL sale, Alfredo Macia, head of Panama's privatization program, told Reuters.
"The decision is still on the table. Some say it should be operating to bring more money for the (INTEL) sale. Others say we should wait and let the new operator run it," Macia said.
"If we think we can pull it off in the next two or three months, we'll do it," he said.
Macia did not say when the government will make the decision. "We're still evaluating," he said.
A consortium led by U.S. telecommunications company BellSouth Corp won the license to build and operate Panama's first cellular telephone network in January with a bid of $72.61 million.
